status: SCHEMA ESTABLISHED AND VERIFIED; TOKEN COUNTS NOT MEASURED
why_counts_not_measured: The orchestrator halted all datasets-server traffic mid-run (the 429 quota is per-IP and 13 agent processes were saturating it). The sampling run was killed after 1 config header and 0 completed configs. Per-config token figures below are therefore CARD values, cross-checked against cheap metadata endpoints already fetched, and are explicitly NOT marked measured.
schema_note: CONFIRMED BY DIRECT QUERY, NOT ASSUMED. The rewrite is at `rollout_results[0].text`. Full shape: FinePhrase carries 12 columns = the 11 columns of its FineWeb-Edu parent plus `rollout_results`. `rollout_results` is a LIST of STRUCT{finish_reason: string, text: string, usage: STRUCT{completion_tokens: int64, prompt_tokens: int64, prompt_tokens_details: null, total_tokens: int64}} -- verified against /info `dataset_info.features` for configs math, table and tutorial (all three byte-identical schemas) and against /first-rows for faq and all. Exactly ONE rollout per document, always: /statistics reports column `rollout_results` with column_type=list and mean=median=min=max=1.0 over 842,000 rows, and all 34 faq rows sampled had len(rollout_results)==1. So element [0] is the entire payload and there is no multi-rollout aggregation to perform. THE TRAP IS REAL AND CONFIRMED: the top-level `text` column holds the ORIGINAL, UNREPHRASED FineWeb-Edu document -- its sibling `dataset` field reads the literal string 'HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu' in 34/34 rows sampled, and `token_count` is FineWeb-Edu's own count of `text` (measured dolma2/token_count ratio 1.0091 on the original, i.e. token_count describes the ORIGINAL, never the rewrite). Counting `text` would build a corpus of unrephrased real web data labelled synthetic, at 27x the true token volume, and neither a size check nor a hash check can detect it because both the bytes and the digest would be internally consistent.
recount_py_verdict: CANNOT REACH IT -- empirically confirmed, not inferred. recount.py `measure()` does `text = row.get(chosen_col)` guarded by `if not isinstance(text, str)`; `--text-column` accepts a column NAME and cannot express a path into a list-of-structs. Ran `recount.py HuggingFaceFW/finephrase --config math --text-column rollout_results`: returned `status: FAILED` with empty tok_counts, because every row yields a list and every row increments n_empty_text. Worse, WITHOUT --text-column its `pick_text_column()` finds `text` via the TEXT_COLUMNS known-name path and returns chosen_by='known-name' -- the highest-confidence label the tool emits -- while silently measuring the original document. A replacement was written and its extractor unit-tested offline (see files_written); it has NOT been run against the API.

short_rewrite_stats.n_caveat: n=34, ONE config (faq), and CRITICALLY these are the first 34 rows of the split (a /first-rows head), NOT random offsets. Parquet row order is content-clustered, so this is a biased head sample. Treat every number here as an UPPER BOUND on the corpus-wide short-rewrite rate, not an estimate of it.

degenerate_examples_verbatim.text: What is the Q&A document about?

1
What is a table dihedral style?

short_rewrite_stats.finish_reason_significance: ALL 34 degenerate outputs have finish_reason='stop'. The generator terminated cleanly and believes it succeeded. `finish_reason` is therefore USELESS as a quality filter -- length is the only available signal.
short_rewrite_stats.design_doc_claim_status: CONFIRMED AND EXCEEDED. The design doc reports one observed 12-token rewrite; the head sample contains three 2-token rewrites, one of which is the bare string 'No answer' -- a refusal, and 'Document:' is a prompt-echo artifact. These are not short documents, they are generation failures with no content at all.
short_rewrite_stats.quality_filtering_verdict: LOAD-BEARING AND MANDATORY. Degenerate rewrites are frequent enough in at least one region of the corpus to matter, they carry a clean finish_reason, and the sibling `text` column means a naive pipeline would paper over them by counting the original instead. A minimum-token filter on rollout_results[0].text is required before publish; a refusal/prompt-echo string blocklist ('No answer', 'Document:', 'A:') is advisable on top. NOTE the tension: the head sample's ~437-vs-41 tokens/doc gap against both the card and the byte arithmetic means the head is anomalously degenerate -- so sizing the filter's yield from these numbers would be wrong. Re-sample at random offsets before choosing a threshold.

all_config_verdict.question: Is `all` a union of 4 independent corpora or 4 correlated views of the same documents?
all_config_verdict.answer: FOUR CORRELATED VIEWS OF THE SAME DOCUMENTS. Confirmed from the repo's own config declaration, not inferred.
evidence: cardData declares config `all` as data_files path = ['faq/**/*.parquet','math/**/*.parquet','table/**/*.parquet','tutorial/**/*.parquet'] -- literally the concatenation of the other four configs. It is a SUPERSET by construction, and adds no data of its own.

Card: 'Source documents in input split: 339,347,842'; 'Output samples across all configs: 1,354,044,711'. 4 x 339,347,842 = 1,357,391,368, and 1,354,044,711 / 1,357,391,368 = 99.75% -- i.e. essentially every source document was rephrased once per format, with a 0.25% generation-failure shortfall.
Per-config row counts are near-identical (338.7M / 338.5M / 337.7M / 339.0M), as expected if each is one pass over the same parent set.
Source is FineWeb-Edu config sample-350BT, a single fixed sample -- the same 339M documents feed all four prompt families.
all_config_verdict.consequence: The advertised 486.4B is NOT 486.4B of independent tokens. It is ~339M source documents seen 4 times through 4 different prompts. Drawing 15B from each of the four formats means the SAME underlying documents appear up to 4 times in our mix, in 4 different surface forms. That is near-duplicate content that no digest-level dedup will catch, because the surface strings genuinely differ. Do NOT treat the four formats as independent sources when computing effective source diversity, and do not use `all` -- draw from the four named configs so the composition is explicit.

meets_3x_peak_demand_note: Peak plausible demand is 6B (30% of a 20B run); 3x = 18B. Even the SMALLEST config (table, 92.4B card / 95.5B byte-implied) exceeds 18B on its own by ~5x. The 15B-per-format plan needs 15B from each of four configs, and the smallest available is 92.4B -- a 6.2x margin on the tightest one. This verdict survives being wrong about the card by a wide factor and does not depend on the halted sampling run.
fifteen_B_per_format_note: YES for all four formats, with >=6x headroom each, on card figures corroborated to 3-9% by independent byte arithmetic. Caveat: 15B of REWRITE tokens. At the card-implied ~273-437 tokens/doc, 15B needs ~34-55M documents per format, i.e. 10-16% of each config -- comfortable. But if the true mean is nearer the head sample's 41 tokens/doc, 15B would need ~366M documents, MORE than the config contains. The byte arithmetic says the card is right and the head is anomalous, so this is very likely fine; a random-offset re-sample is what would close it.
overlaps: CRITICAL, FLAGGED PER THE BRIEF: FinePhrase is a rephrasing of HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu (config sample-350BT, split train) -- stated on the card and confirmed by the per-row `dataset` field reading 'HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu'. It therefore OVERLAPS every FineWeb-lineage real-token source in the reservoir at the DOCUMENT level: FineWeb-Edu itself, FineWeb-Edu-score-2, FineWeb, and (per README.md item 2's lineage chain) Zyda-2 and anything else containing FineWeb-Edu-score-2. Do not sum synthetic FinePhrase tokens against FineWeb-lineage real tokens as if they were disjoint pools.

The overlap is not merely lineage bookkeeping: every FinePhrase document's ORIGINAL text is physically present in the corpus as the `text` column. If any part of the pipeline ever reads the wrong column, we ingest FineWeb-Edu twice -- once as real, once as 'synthetic'.

Rephrasing defeats n-gram decontamination (see project memory: rephrased synthetic hides contamination). FineWeb-Edu does zero decontam and this pipeline has none either, so FinePhrase inherits and then CONCEALS whatever eval contamination FineWeb-Edu carries.
Internal overlap: the four formats are 4 views of one 339M-document set -- see all_config_verdict. Cross-format near-duplication is structural, not incidental.
needs_streaming_count: HuggingFaceFW/finephrase/faq -- datasets-server cannot serve it at all (/size job failed, /rows 500, /info 500; only /first-rows responds). Its 339,039,447 row count is derived by subtraction and its 148.1B is card-only. Needs a Batch streaming count or a parquet footer read.
HuggingFaceFW/finephrase/all -- same 500s. Lower priority: it is a declared superset of the other four and should not be published or drawn from directly.

HuggingFaceFW/finephrase/{math,table,tutorial} -- countable via /rows once the per-IP 429 quota is free; the tool to do it is written, offline-tested, and ready. Run `recount_finephrase.py --configs math,table,tutorial --n-sample 200`, serially, when no other agent is holding the quota.

ALL FOUR need a random-offset short-rewrite re-sample before a quality-filter threshold is chosen -- the n=34 head sample is demonstrably unrepresentative (41 vs ~437 tokens/doc against two independent non-sampled routes).

files_written.artifacts/recount/recount_finephrase.py: standalone nested-payload counter. Extracts rollout_results[0].text, tokenizes rewrite AND original from the same rows (so the ratio is paired), reuses recount.py's bootstrap_ci and load_tokenizer by import rather than copy, and uses a card-anchored estimator (exact whole-corpus completion_tokens x sampled dolma2/completion-token ratio) as an independent cross-check on the sample mean -- because /statistics publishes no char mean for a string nested in a list, so recount.py's stats-ratio factoring is unavailable here. Retries HTTP 429 with backoff and persists after every config. Its extractor is unit-tested offline against the 34 cached rows (34/34, never returns the original, handles 4 degenerate inputs); the HTTP path is UNVALIDATED -- the run was killed before any config completed.
